newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Newmont set to start on major Indonesia gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Newmont set to start on major Indonesia gold mine.

text.p: Newmont Gold Company is set to start construction of a major new copper and gold mine in Indonesia, a company official said Wednesday.
"The final (government) environmental approval for the project is imminent, and we should kick off construction soon," Newmont Gold Vice-President Eric Hamer told Reuters in an interview.

The mine, on the southwest corner of Sumbawa island, will be operated by PT Newmont Nusa Tenggara, in which Newmont has a 45 percent stake. Japan's Sumitomo Corp. has 35 percent and Indonesian miner PT Pukuafu Indah holds 20 percent.

Hamer said production at the Sumbawa mine would start in 1999. It was expected to reach an annual output of more than 500,000 ounces of gold and 250,000 tons of copper concentrate during its 20-year lifespan.
A total of 5,500 people would be employed during the peak construction period, and the mine would employ 2,200 people when operating.

Hamer described the ore body as "low grade, high tonnage," with current reserves of 13.4 million ounces of gold and 5.3 million tons of copper. "This is the biggest single gold-bearing deposit Newmont has found in its history," he said.
"We think there's a lot more ore further down that will extend the mine's life," Hamer added.
Hamer said the estimated capital cost of the project was $1.6 billion, rising to $1.9 billion with capitalised interest for the loans.
